column1: # The ONE fixture both ratchet readers are driven against (claude-config#377).
# There are two implementations, one in bash and one in python, because two of the guards that use
# them are shell suites and two are python scans, and neither language can call the other's reader
# without paying a process per run. Twin implementations in two languages consume one shared
# committed fixture, or they agree on the day they are written and nowhere after it (L26).
# One case per line, tab separated:
#   <name>  <baseline text, \n for a newline>  <measured text, \n for a newline>  <verdict>
# measured is the same shape as a baseline: what a fresh scan found. verdict is one of
#   ok       nothing grew and nothing is stale
#   grown    a path measures higher than recorded, which is the fault these exist to catch
#   stale    a path measures lower than recorded, so the number has to come down (L182)
#   both     one path grew and another is stale, in the same run
# A reader that reports only the first of those two would pass every case but this one.
a clean run
a path that grew
a path that appeared
a path that shrank
a path that went to zero
a path that vanished
one of each at once
an empty baseline and nothing found
an empty baseline and something found
comments and blank lines are not entries
whitespace around the count is not a value
a zero recorded and a zero found
a path with a slash in it
